==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|shew||archaic}} * {{alt|en|shewe|showe||obsolete}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ʃəʊ/|a=RP}} * {{enPR|shō|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/ʃoʊ/}} * {{IPA|en|[ʃoː]|[ʃow]|a=CA}} * {{IPA|en|/ʃo(w)/|/ʃɔw/|a=Indic}} * {{IPA|en|/ʃəʊ/|a=IE}} ** {{IPA|en|/ʃʌo̞/|a=Dublin}} * {{audio|en|en-us-show.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|En-uk-to show.ogg|a=London}} * {{rhymes|en|əʊ|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:schewen|id=to display|tree=+}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)kewh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|schewen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|scēawian||to look, look at, exhibit, display}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skauwōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*skawwōną|t=to look, see}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)kewh₁-||to heed, look, feel, take note of}}; see {{m|en|haw}}, {{m|en|gaum}}, {{m|en|caveat}}, {{m|en|caution}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|shaw||to show}}, {{cog|nl|schouwen||to inspect, view}}, {{cog|de|schauen||to see, behold}}, {{cog|da|skue||to behold}}. Related to {{l|en|sheen}}. Wider cognates include {{cog|grc|κῦδος}}, {{cog|la|caveō}} whence {{cog|en|caution}} and {{m|en|caveat}}, {{cog|sa|कवि|tr=kaví||seer, prophet, bard}}, {{cog|sla-pro|*čuti}} (whence {{cog|ru|чу́ять}} and many more). ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|+,shew|~n,~ed}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[display]], [[convey]] or [[exhibit]]; to have something available for others to [[see]]; to direct attention to something. #: {{ux|en|The king '''showed''' great wisdom in his decisions.}} #: {{ux|en|The actor '''showed''' Macbeth's confidence in this scene.}} #: {{ux|en|The car's dull finish '''showed''' years of neglect.}} #: {{ux|en|All he had to '''show''' for four years of attendance at college was a framed piece of paper.}} #: {{ux|en|I do some sculpturing, but I don't like to '''show''' anybody.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=22|passage=Not unnaturally, “Auntie” took this communication in bad part. Thus outraged, she '''showed''' herself to be a bold as well as a furious virago. Next day she found her way to their lodgings and tried to recover her ward by the hair of the head.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[indicate]]; to convey facts that lead to a conclusion. ##: {{ux|en|The record '''shows''' that you have been late twelve times this year.}} ##: {{ux|en|Our schedule is '''showing''' appointments all day.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[guide]] or [[escort]]; to [[show the way]]. ##: {{ux|en|Could you please '''show''' him on his way. He has overstayed his welcome.}} ##: {{ux|en|Who can '''show''' me to the office? I'll '''show''' you in.}} ##: {{ux|en|If you get aggressive, the bouncer will '''show''' you to the door.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[bestow]]; to [[confer]]. ##: {{ux|en|to '''show''' mercy; to '''show''' favour}} ##: {{ux|en|{{lb|en|dialectal}} '''show''' me the salt please}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To put on a movie, TV show, etc; to be presented in this way. ##: {{ux|en|The cinema on Ninth Avenue is '''showing''' a couple family movies.}} ##: {{ux|en|They '''showed''' episodes of some awful TV show on our flight.}} ##: {{ux|en|The new Brad Pitt movie is '''showing''' at eight o'clock tonight.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To display [[artwork]] in a [[gallery]] or [[museum]]. ##: {{ux|en|John is '''showing''' his work tonight.}} ##: {{ux|en|The Smithsonian '''shows''' most of that artist's work.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To display on offer. ##: {{ux|en|The store on Eighth Street is '''showing''' the new spring collection in the window.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|card games}} To give hints to the apparent or purported nature of one's hand of cards. ##: {{ux|en|There's a bunch of ways to '''show''' a bad hand.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|card games}} To reveal one's hand of cards. ##: {{ux|en|He just wanted to finish this hand, so he '''showed''' as soon as he could.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2017|author=Nathan Schwiethale|title=Ace High: Mastering Low Stakes Poker Cash Games|page=70 |passage=He called instantly but was too ashamed to '''show''' until the river.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|or|transitive}} To participate in a [[dog show]], [[cat show]], etc.; to compete with an animal at such a show; to be entered and displayed at such a show. ##: {{ux|en|That's why we don't '''show''' in Philadelphia anymore.}} ##: {{ux|en|She's '''showing''' her poodle at the dog show.}} ##: {{ux|en|Nibbles is '''showing''' at the California Cat Show.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To prove (a fact) to be true; to [[demonstrate]]; to [[instruct]]. #: {{ux|en|We '''showed''' that the hypothesis is correct.}} #: {{ux|en|She is '''showing''' how to complete the task.}} #: {{ux|en|He doesn't just tell you how to do it, he '''shows''' you.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2012|month=March-April |author=John T. Jost|volume=100|issue=2|page=162|magazine=w:American Scientist |title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/social-justice-is-it-in-our-nature-and-our-future Social Justice: Is It in Our Nature (and Our Future)?] |passage=He draws eclectically on studies of baboons, descriptive anthropological accounts of hunter-gatherer societies and, in a few cases, the fossil record. With this biological framework in place, Corning endeavors to '''show''' that the capitalist system as currently practiced in the United States and elsewhere is manifestly unfair.}} ## {{lb|en|reflexive|or|transitive}} To reveal one's condition or nature. ##: {{ux|en|She '''showed''' herself to be a jerk.}} ##: {{ux|en|That '''shows''' what kind of person he is.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|usually emphasized|sometimes with the placeholder pronoun ''it''}} To demonstrate to another that they are wrong; to vindicate to someone; to prove something to those who doubt it; to suffice as revenge against someone. ##: {{ux|en|She doesn't think I can win, so if I do, that'll '''show''' her.}} ##: {{ux|en|I'll prove your innocence to '''show''' it to your accusers.}} ##: {{ux|en|This experiment will '''show''' that my theory is right.}} ##: {{ux|en|If he attacked you, I'll kick his ass. Getting beat up will '''show''' him.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be or become [[visible]] or [[apparent]]; to be [[seen]] or [[demonstrated]]; to [[appear]] or be made to appear. #: {{ux|en|That wine stain '''shows''' on your shirt. You should wear a jacket to cover it up, so it doesn't '''show'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Your bald patch is starting to '''show'''.}} #: {{ux|en|His experience '''showed''', because he knew exactly what to do when the emergency happened.}} #: {{ux|en|Her hatred '''showed''' on her face.}} #: {{ux|en|Staining wood will make minor scratches '''show''' on the surface.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Don Sebastian|passage=Just such she '''shows''' before a rising storm.}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson Poems 1842|volume=II|poem=The Day-Dream|section=The Sleeping Palace|page=151|passage=All round a hedge upshoots, and '''shows''' / At distance like a little wood.}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=1|passage='Twas early June, the new grass was flourishing everywheres, the posies in the yard—peonies and such—in full bloom, the sun was shining, and the water of the bay was blue, with light green streaks where the shoal '''showed'''.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1989|month=May|volume=175|number=5|title=Braving the Northwest Passage|author=Jeff MacInnis|page=600 |text=The strain of the long voyage '''shows''' in our faces, but there is no disguising our joy.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|informal}} To put in an appearance; [[show up]]. ##: {{ux|en|Nobody even '''showed''' at our party.}} ##: {{ux|en|We waited for an hour, but they never '''showed''', so we had to take the bus home.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To finish third in a race, especially in horse or dog racing. ##: {{ux|en|In the third race: Aces Up won, paying eight dollars; Blarney Stone placed, paying three dollars; and Cinnamon '''showed''', paying five dollars.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To come into view on a screen; to become visible on a screen. ##: {{ux|en|An error message will '''show''' on your monitor.}} ##: {{ux|en|A color fluctuation will '''show''' on your computer screen.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|informal}} To have an enlarged [[belly]] and thus be recognizable as [[pregnant]]. ##: {{ux|en|She's not '''showing''' yet, so I didn't realize she was pregnant.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|copulative|archaic}} To [[appear]] (a certain way). ##: {{ux|en|He '''showed''' tired after a long day's toil.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|title=In The Heart Of The Storm|volume=1|author=Maxwell Grey|year=1891|text={{...}} until the grey wintry dawn paled them, and the chill earth '''showed''' ghostly and desolate in the cold light.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To appear or suit; to reflect well or poorly on someone; to be fitting. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-2|act=IV|scene=i|passage=My lord of York, it better '''showed''' with you.}} =====Usage notes===== * The past participle ''shown'' was uncommon before the 19th century, but is now the preferred form in standard English. In the UK, ''showed'' is regarded as archaic or dialectal. In the US, it is considered a standard variant form, but ''shown'' is more common. ''Garner's Modern American Usage'' favors ''shown'' over ''showed'' as past participle and claims it is mandatory for passives. * In the past, {{m|en|shew}} was used as a past-tense form and {{m|en|shewed}} as a past participle of this verb; both forms are now archaic. =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|old=1|past_ptc=shown}} =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|display}} {{l|en|display}},
